**Visual observations:**
- Young corn plant (early vegetative stage, ~V3-V4) lying completely flat on bare soil
- Plant has collapsed — the whole plant is prostrate
- Leaves still appear green (not yet dried out), suggesting sudden/recent collapse
- Stem/base area shows some darkening/discoloration where the plant collapsed
- No visible leaf lesions, rust pustules, mold, or smut galls
- Collapse appears to originate at the base/lower internode

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Bacterial_stalk_rot**: "Affected plants suddenly collapse and fall over with their vascular strands still intact." First/second internode above soil becomes water-soaked, soft, and mushy causing sudden collapse. Young plants affected. This matches perfectly — sudden collapse of a young green plant at the base.
- **Physoderma_stalk_rot**: Would show black nodes and break at node — no clearly black nodes visible.
- **Anthracnose_stalk_rot**: Shiny black rind discoloration, typically in more mature plants post-pollination.
- **Diplodia_stalk_rot**: Shredded pith with black pycnidia, mature plants.
- **Crazy_top**: Would show twisted leaves, bushy tassel mass — not present.

The sudden, complete collapse of a young green corn plant at the base internode with no visible leaf disease is the hallmark of **Bacterial_stalk_rot**.
